reading.body:
DartPoints Baton Rouge 1 publishes 2.5 MW of IT capacity. At 10 kW per rack, a common colocation density for enterprise workloads, that is roughly 250 racks; at 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, it is roughly 63 racks. The arithmetic is an assumption, not an operator claim. No certifications are listed in the published specifications, so no statement about qualifying workloads can be made from that angle.

Louisiana has four mapped facilities in this site's dataset, three of which publish a megawatt figure, totaling 7.7 MW across those three. DartPoints Baton Rouge 1 contributes 2.5 MW of that total, which is roughly 32 percent, and ranks second by published IT capacity among the state's facilities this site has read. The state's total published figure is small relative to major US data center markets, and most mapped Louisiana facilities publish no capacity figure at all, so the true installed base is larger than 7.7 MW by an unknown amount.

For a reader deciding whether this campus matters to AI, the published scale answers the question directly: 2.5 MW of IT capacity is suited to inference at modest throughput or to regional edge deployments, not to large-scale AI training, which typically requires tens to hundreds of megawatts in a single facility. The campus may serve as a low-latency access point for the Gulf Coast region, but that is a geographic inference, not a published claim. No tenants, pricing, or power source details are published on the operator's specification page this site has read.
